extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, organizations, and institutional applicants seeking grants from the W. M. Keck Foundation (Research Program, Southern California Program, Special Projects)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for applying to the W. M. Keck Foundation's Research, Southern California, and Special Projects grant programs, including program priorities, submission portals, concept review windows, and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research program focus / priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting pioneering discoveries in science, engineering and medical research to generate far-reaching benefits for humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation funds high-impact, pioneering scientific, engineering, and medical research with potential for broad benefit to humanity (the 'Keck Effect'). Applicants should align proposals with this emphasis on pioneering, far-reaching impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Projects focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Major grants with potential for extraordinary impact invited by the W. M. Keck Foundation Board of Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special Projects are board-invited and target proposals that promise extraordinary, large-scale impact. These are distinct from open Research or Southern California program solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Southern California program focus / priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting the healthy development of children and youth, strengthening families, and enriching the lives of people in the Southern California region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to the Southern California Program should be regionally focused and advance child and youth development, family strengthening, or community enrichment in Southern California.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and concept requests must be submitted via the Foundation portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions (Concept requests, Phase I applications, full applications) are submitted through the Foundation's online portal. The site repeatedly states 'Applications must be submitted via the Foundation portal.' Follow the portal's instructions; other submission methods are not indicated as acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and time-of-day requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific program deadlines and cutoffs (date and time) must be observed; many deadlines are 4:30pm (PT) on the listed date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I and other application deadlines are posted with exact dates and a 4:30pm PT cutoff (examples shown: Phase I deadlines May 1 and November 3; Southern California application deadlines Jan 5 and July 1). Early submissions are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept review / concept counseling process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation runs concept review windows during which concept requests are submitted and reviewed; counseling requests were scheduled on a first-come, first-served basis when held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept review windows open and close on posted dates (examples given). Concept requests must be submitted via the portal. The page notes updated concept guidelines and also indicates the Research Program is rolling out a new process (including changes to concept counseling). Applicants should consult the current Concept Guidelines and Research Process Overview for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific eligibility and application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program (Research, Southern California, Special Projects) has eligibility rules and application instructions available on its program pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult the Program Overview, Eligibility, and Application Instructions pages for program-specific requirements; the homepage links to those pages but does not reproduce detailed eligibility criteria. Current Grantees and Liaison Guidelines pages are also available for related procedural information.
